mappings.note: Defines the alkane, alkene and alkyne series and places C4H10 in one of them (C 1.1-LO-4), then asks for two structural isomers of it (C 1.3-LO-4). Both demands are separately marked.
Ethanol named from alcoholic drinks, two uses, and its reactions with sodium and with hot conc. H2SO4 - all four parts are properties of the named compound, LO-8.

Three distinct demands in one item: the electron dot structure of methane (C 1.3-LO-4), why covalent compounds conduct poorly and melt low (C 1.1, since no outcome covers those properties), and what happens when methane burns (C 1.3, since combustion has no outcome).

Part (a) is the poor-conductor gap (C 1.1); part (b) asks for the name and structure of cyclohexane (C 1.3-LO-4). The single-bond count rides on the drawn ring rather than standing alone, so C 1.1-LO-3 is not added.
Identification chain resting on ethanol's dehydration and its reaction with sodium - both LO-8 properties.
Counts the distinct ways of building C6H14, i.e. its five structural isomers - the isomer clause of C 1.3-LO-4.
Draws every isomer of C3H6O and their electron dot structures. Both halves of C 1.3-LO-4 (structural formulae plus electron dot structures, and isomers) in a single item, so one code suffices.
Which of C3H8 and C3H6 adds, plus hydrogenation in the vanaspati industry. Addition reactions have no outcome in this frame; C 1.3 competency cited.
Chemical tests for ethanol and for ethanoic acid, and why the acid is called glacial - properties of the two compounds LO-8 names.
Defines micelles and explains how they lift dirt - 'cleansing action of soaps and micelle formation' is LO-9 word for word.

Defines an oxidising agent and applies it to PROPANOL, not ethanol. LO-8 names only ethanol and ethanoic acid, so it does not reach this homologue; the item is really about the oxidation reaction class, which sits under C 1.3.
Esterification with the class of product and the role of conc. H2SO4 - esterification is named in LO-8.
Duplicate of sha 5dfb96f368c878ee (same esterification item, one extra worked example in the answer). Mapped identically.

Ethanol's dehydration and the ester's use are LO-8; the reason the two compounds behave differently is that their functional groups differ, which is C 1.1-LO-4. Both are needed because the functional-group argument is the graded point of part (i).
Part (a) defines and identifies functional groups (C 1.1-LO-4); part (b) is the alkaline KMnO4 oxidation of ethanol and the reagent's role (C 1.2-LO-8).

Deduces from the sodium test that C3H8O carries an -OH group (C 1.1-LO-4) and then writes its structure (C 1.3-LO-4). LO-8 is not cited because the compound is propanol, which the outcome does not name.
Dehydration of ethanol with the role of conc. H2SO4 (LO-8), then hydrogenation of the ethene formed (C 1.3, addition having no outcome).
Three routes from ethanoic acid to sodium ethanoate (NaOH, Na, Na2CO3) - all chemical properties of the named acid, LO-8.
Identifies glacial acetic acid from its freezing behaviour and forms the ester with ethanol - a melting point and an esterification, both LO-8.
Changes (i) and (ii) are ethanol and ethanoic acid chemistry (LO-8); change (iii), methane to chloromethane, is a substitution with no outcome, hence C 1.3.

Part (a) denatured alcohol, a property/use of ethanol (LO-8); part (b) the seven covalent bonds of ethane, which is the tetravalency-plus-catenation count of LO-3. The structure is drawn only to justify the count, so C 1.3-LO-4 is not added.
Equations (i) and (ii) are the ethanol oxidation and the saponification of an ester (LO-8); equation (iii) is the methane/chlorine substitution, which falls to C 1.3.
Identifies ethanol and ethanoic acid from wine and vinegar (LO-8) and explicitly demands both structural formulae (C 1.3-LO-4).
Two unrelated halves stapled together: draw ethyne (C 1.3-LO-4) and list two soap-versus-detergent differences (C 1.2-LO-9).

Parts (i)-(iii) are the definition of a homologous series and the gradation of physical versus chemical properties along it (C 1.1-LO-4); part (iv) asks for the names AND structures of the C3H6O aldehyde and ketone (C 1.3-LO-4).
